metadata.title: Addendum to "Geodesic fields for Pontryagin type $C^0$-Finsler manifolds"
metadata.abstract: In the paper ``Geodesic fields for Pontryagin type $C^0$-Finsler manifolds'', the same authors introduced a geometric object called Pontryagin-type $C^0$-Finsler structures, which includes Finsler structures on a smooth manifold $M$. Such a structure is defined locally by a control system of $C^1$ unit vector fields on an open subset $U$ of $M$, such that Pontryagin's maximum principle (PMP) is applicable. As a result of PMP, we obtain the extended geodesic field $\mathcal{E}$, which is a multivalued vector field on the slit cotangent bundle $T^{\ast}U\backslash 0 = \{(x,\alpha): x\in U, \alpha \in T^{\ast}_x U\}$, such that every minimizing path $x(t)$ on $(U,F)$ is an extremal (projection of a Pontryagin extremal $(x(t),\alpha(t))$). Some time after its introduction, its use and external comments, it is useful to provide remarks that clarify the applicability and limitations of this theory. In addition, we point out two errors contained in that work which, although discernible from the context, we believe should be pointed out. Finally, we prove some cases where the property that a minimizing path is the projection of a Pontryagin extremal can be extended beyond a coordinate system, sometimes to $M$. We also work on the problem of determining when $\mathcal{E}$ does not depend on the control system chosen to represent $F$. In particular, $\mathcal{E}$ satisfies these two properties globally for left-invariant $C^0$-Finsler structures on Lie groups, and for $C^1$-Finsler structures (without the condition of strong convexity).
